rules.name: Teaching Requirement for Both Tracks
rules.desc:
Teaching is core to the academic and professional training of doctoral students in our program. All students are required to complete 1 quarter of teaching experience by the end of their 2nd year in the program regardless of their financial support. Typically, students complete more than the required number of teaching quarters as part of their professional training and financial support.
Teaching Requirement for Both Tracks

• Attend a Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL) teaching assistant training orientation

• International students who were required to submit TOEFL scores as part of their Stanford graduate program application must be approved for English proficiency through the TA Screening process prior to being appointed as a teaching assistant.

• Attend department training for Teaching Assistantship

rules.name: Research Requirements
rules.desc:
Research is core to the academic and professional training of doctoral students in our program.
In the 1st year, complete the following requirements:

• By Course Withdrawal Deadline in the spring quarter, confirm attendance and participation in the department review of ethics workshop

• As scheduled by the department, attend the department ethics workshop to review ethics in Anthropology.

• By Course Withdrawal Deadline in the spring quarter, complete the appropriate CITI tutorial for Responsible Conduct of Research

• Complete the appropriate CITI tutorial for non-medical human subjects, and either submit a non-medical human subjects protocol, based on the pre-dissertation research proposal, to the Institutional Review Board before departing for summer quarter field research in the first year or confirm approval for exempt status. Alternatively, a notice of determination may be confirmed with the Institutional Review Board for a pilot study proposal that does not require protocol submission.

• By the first day of finals week in spring quarter, receive final approval for the Summer Research Proposal

In the 2nd year, complete the following requirements:

• By the first day of finals week in spring quarter, must receive final approval for Pre-Dissertation Research Proposal
In the 3rd year, complete the following requirements:
Autumn Quarter

• By the first day of finals week, third-year students must submit three draft dissertation research funding proposals to the faculty advisor for approval.
Spring Quarter

• By Course Withdrawal Deadline in the spring quarter, must receive final approval of the Dissertation Proposal

• Before departing for field research students should receive approval for the non-medical human subjects protocol from the Institutional Review Board.
Summer Quarter

• By the end of summer quarter in the third year, submit approved external funding proposal to at least three different funding agencies (e.g. Wenner Gren).
In the 4th year, complete the following requirements:

• Conduct at least nine months of approved dissertation field research under the Dissertation Reading Committee’s (DRC) supervision.

• By the end of the summer quarter of the fourth year, fourth-year students submit the 4th Year PhD Checklist confirming date of return from fieldwork

• Upon completion and return from field research submit a report of the degree progress to the DRC.

Additional details on Research Procedures can be found in the Graduate Handbook https://anthropology.stanford.edu/intranet-login/graduate-student-center.

rules.name: Advancement to Candidacy
rules.desc:
Admission to candidacy is a prospective judgement by the faculty of a student’s potential to successfully complete the requirements of the degree program. Students are expected to complete qualifying procedures by the last week of classes in the spring quarter, and apply for candidacy by the end of Winter. Qualifying procedures in the Department of Anthropology include required coursework, identification of an advisor by the end of the first year of the program, approval of the pre-dissertation proposal, demonstration of the ability to conduct independent research, analysis and interpretation, and completion of degree milestones of the first and second year.
Timeline
Winter Quarter:

• By the first day of finals week, submit the Application for Candidacy form.

Spring Quarter:

• By the Course Withdrawal Deadline, submit the 2nd Year PhD Checklist with the final draft of the research proposal. The date for submission of the final draft of the research proposal in spring quarter will be determined by the faculty instructor for the required proposal writing course for either the Archaeology track ANTHRO308A or the Culture and Society track ANTHRO308

• Failure to advance to candidacy will result in the student’s dismissal from the PhD degree program.

Additional details on candidacy procedures can be found in the Graduate Handbookhttps://anthropology.stanford.edu/intranet-login/graduate-student-

rules.name: University Oral Exam (Dissertation Defense)
rules.desc:
Quarter before scheduled Oral Examination

• Obtain approval for the final draft status of the dissertation using the 5th Year Dissertation Defense Checklist.

• Notify the student services manager of intent to Graduate

• Schedule defense date with Oral Exam Committee

• At least four weeks before a proposed date for the University Oral Examination

• Submit the University Oral Examination form and evidence of approval for the final draft of the dissertation by the dissertation reading committee to the department.

• Pass the University Oral Examination

• Oral presentation, held at the beginning of the public presentation (approximately 30 minutes for presentation with a 15-minute public discussion period)

• Followed by a closed session with the oral examination committee members, only (approximately 2 hours for the private examination).
Additional details on Oral Exam (Dissertation Defense) procedures can be found in the Graduate Handbook https://anthropology.stanford.edu/intranet-login/graduate-student-center.

rules.name: Dissertation Submission
rules.desc:
After Oral Examination

• Once the University Oral Examination has been passed, submit the final DRC-approved dissertation to the university Registrar via Axess (Instructions to obtain approval), requesting conferral of the doctoral degree in Anthropology.

rules.name: Language Requirement
rules.desc:
The Anthropology PhD language requirement ensures oral and reading proficiency in a language necessary for successful scholarship in a chosen field of study.
First Year

• By the course withdrawal deadline in spring quarter, submit a Draft Foreign Language Plan detailing a draft language plan of study or requesting approval for satisfactory completion.
Second Year

• By the first day of finals week in winter quarter of the Second year, submit an Updated Foreign Language Plan detailing an updated language plan of study or requesting approval for satisfactory completion.
The language requirement may be met via:

• Academic, immersion, or homestay program for language study; or,

• Tutoring or distance language study; or,

• Foreign Language and Area Studies Fellowships (FLAS)-related or other programs supporting language study.

gpa: Ph.D. Students in Anthropology must complete a minimum of 135 quarter units with a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B).
grading: All required courses in Anthropology appropriate for the student’s chosen track must be passed with a minimum grade of B+.
transferPolicy: Students who completed graduate coursework at another institution can transfer course units after completing one quarter of enrollment. The Anthropology Graduate Program Committee will evaluate the transfer of units on a course-by-course basis. Graduate work accepted for transfer of residency does not automatically exempt a student from having to complete a course requirement for the degree
reviewNotes: You pick the Archaeology or Culture and Society track. Its required courses need a B+ or better, and its electives (four for Archaeology, three for Culture and Society) are 5 units each and letter graded. The audit also checks ANTHRO 310G and 444 for three quarters each, the third-year qualifying exam courses, ANTHRO 802 once you are TGR, and 135 graduate units. The 3.0 GPA and every yearly checklist, teaching, research, language, candidacy, exam and dissertation milestone are checked by hand.
